newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bel-20 sets record, but outlook uncertain.
newsitem.headline: Bel-20 sets record, but outlook uncertain.

text.p: Belgian shares headed further into record territory on Wednesday, but the outlook for Thursday was uncertain after late afternoon comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan sent the Dow .DJI lower.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended 7.13 points or 0.33 percent firmer at a closing high of 2,145.43, with a lower-than-average 2.6 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
"The Brussels market had no time to react to Wall Street's fall," one dealer said. Greenspan rattled the markets by saying he could not rule out an interest rate rise to fight inflationary risks.
Another dealer said the effect on Wall Street did not appear to be "too negative", and he was fairly optimistic on the Belgian market generally in terms of fundamentals.
Renewed dollar strength was a supportive factor late in the session.
Retail group GIB was a star performer, climbing 4.2 percent to 1,610 francs with 97,730 shares changing hands.
The stock was boosted after Pierre Scohier, chairman of GIB and also of holding company Cobepa, reiterated on Tuesday that GIB was open to strengthening its various business through alliances.
"People are really anxious to have any good news on companies because they lack new ideas. But I'm not sure it might not lead to disappointment when they publish their results," said one dealer.

Dollar-sensitive non-ferrous metals stock Union Miniere extended its recent recovery, up 2.58 percent at 2,585 francs. One dealer noted the stock continued to benefit from good zinc prices. Another said Belgian cyclical stocks generally had enjoyed buying apparently related to a cyclical stocks product created by Kredietbank Petercam Derivatives.
